title: Longest Uncommon Subsequence II
spaceBreakdown:
- isSubseq: uses only index variable i → O(1)
- ans, n, loop counters: O(1) scalars
- not counted: input vector strs
approach: The longest uncommon subsequence must be one of the input strings themselves: if some subsequence of strs[i] is not a subsequence of any other string, then strs[i] itself is also not a subsequence of any other string (if strs[i] were a subsequence of strs[j], then any subsequence of strs[i] would also be a subsequence of strs[j]). So we check each string against every other string using a two-pointer subsequence test, and return the maximum length among strings that are not a subsequence of any other string, or -1 if none qualify.
hints: For each string strs[i], what is the longest subsequence you could possibly form from it? Each strs[i] has length at most 10.

Use a two-pointer subsequence check: for each string, test whether it is a subsequence of every other string. For "abc" vs "aebdc": advance the "abc" pointer on each match (a→e→b→d→c gives a,b,c all matched), so "abc" is a subsequence of "aebdc".

**Self-comparison** - each string is always a subsequence of itself.
`Input: strs = ["aba","cdc","eae"]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: not skipping i==j in the inner loop → isSubseq("aba","aba") is true, every string marked invalid, returns -1

**All duplicates** - every string is a subsequence of its identical copy.
`Input: strs = ["aaa","aaa","aa"]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: initializing ans=0 instead of -1 → returns 0 (the empty string is a subsequence of every string, so no uncommon subsequence exists)

**All identical** - no string is uncommon.
`Input: strs = ["a","a"]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: returning max string length without subsequence check → returns 1

**Subsequence across different lengths** - a shorter string can be a subsequence of a longer one.
`Input: strs = ["a","ab","ab"]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: only comparing strings of equal length → "a" is never checked against "ab", marked valid, returns 1

followUps.q: What if strs.length is up to 10^5 and each string length is up to 10?
followUps.a: Group identical strings with a hash map; any string appearing more than once is automatically invalid (it is a subsequence of its duplicate). For each unique string appearing once, check if it is a subsequence of any other unique string. Sort unique strings by length descending and return the first valid one. TC: O(U² · L) where U is the number of unique strings, SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if you must return the actual longest uncommon subsequence string, not just its length?
followUps.a: The answer is always one of the input strings, so track the string itself alongside its length during the scan. Return the valid string with maximum length, or an empty string if none exist. TC and SC are unchanged.

followUps.q: What if each string length can be up to 10^5 (with strs.length still ≤ 50)?
followUps.a: Precompute a next-position table next[i][c] for each string giving the smallest index j ≥ i where character c appears, enabling subsequence checks in O(|a|) instead of O(|b|). TC: O(n · L · 26 + n² · L) for precomputation and checks, SC: O(n · L · 26) for the tables.
